floor_history.headline: recon: retired body 65 -> recovered WIP score-8 form transfers at 7 on soft-float -> int-typed stride+base sum gives 6; last 6 = sched1 LUID tie between the a2-site init and the call arg loads, proven
Floor holds at 6 (176/176, RA byte-identical to target); 16 structural spellings measured, both banked frontier routes F1 and F2 retired with mechanism cites, residual is a pure 3-insn emission-order

frontier.hypothesis: Our pre-sched1 dependence graph around uids 211 (a2 init), 240 (a0 load), 242 (a1 load) and 205 (the lw) differs from what the target's order requires - most plausibly an anti-dependence our a2 pseudo carries because split-init writes it four times.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 rank_for_schedule (tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c:2464) only reaches the INSN_LUID tie-break when priority and class are equal and the insn is READY; a dependence that delays 211's readiness past clocks 66-67, or one that removes 242/240 from the clock-64 ready set, reproduces the target order without needing luid(211) > 43. s1 already showed 'LAUNCH(211) + 228 depends on 211' hits the target in both halves, so the dependence axis is live even though the LAUNCH prong (H8) is not affordable.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/sched_solver extract.py text1b + simulate.py --func func_8005D554 --pass 1 on the current candidate and dump the full dependence LISTS (not just priorities) for uids 205/211/240/242; then enumerate, in the exact model, which single added or removed dependence flips the clock-64 pick, and only then look for a C spelling that produces exactly that dependence at 176 insns.

frontier.hypothesis: The loop chassis itself (guard-in-i + do-while, inherited unchanged from the 2026-08-05 WIP) is not the target's, and a different loop shape changes the block's dependence graph and register pressure enough to move the residual.
frontier.mechanism: The chassis was selected on the pre-soft-float chassis for the frame +16 (jump.c duplicate_loop_exit_test phantom slot); the frame is now settled at 120 == target, so the shape was never re-justified on this chassis. Note this does NOT evade the H7 class kill - the arg loads are emitted last whatever the loop shape - its value is the dependence/pressure change.
frontier.next_probe: Re-measure a for-loop chassis and a while-loop chassis with the identical body (and with/without the guard duplicated into the loop variable), checking BOTH the frame size and the 12-insn residual; if any keeps frame 120 and changes the residual shape, re-run pairdiff and the pass-1 simulation on it.

frontier.hypothesis: r4 (the loop-invariant (D_800A3418 * 0xDC) >> 0xF computed before the loop) is not the carrier the target subtracts from, and a different but semantically identical source expression for the a2 base lands its insn elsewhere in the RTL stream.
frontier.mechanism: The target's addiu a2,s4,-K reads s4 which our build also assigns to r4, so any alternative must be arithmetically identical; but the RTL position of the subtraction is fixed by which tree node expand walks it from, and s1/s2 only ever spelled it as a subtraction off a plain local.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate arithmetically identical spellings of the a2 base that expand from a different tree shape - e.g. r4 held in a second invariant local written once before the loop, the subtraction expressed as an addition of a negative constant, or the base carried as a pointer displacement - and measure each with sandbox; any that keeps 176/176 and moves the addiu is worth a pass-1 simulation.
